established_findings.statement: LLMs can produce draft network configurations from high-level intent but produce syntax, topology, and semantic errors when used alone; combining LLM generation with deterministic verifiers and localized feedback substantially reduces errors and yields verified configurations.
limitations: Experiments are limited in scope (few use cases/protocols).
Human-in-the-loop input remained required in reported studies.
Model versions and prompt details vary across studies, limiting direct comparability.

established_findings.statement: Deterministic network-verification tools (e.g., Header Space Analysis, NetPlumber, VeriFlow) can check network state and configuration changes rapidly and are suitable validators to detect correctness/failure modes of generated configurations.
limitations: Verification effectiveness depends on precise formal specifications; not all higher-level intent properties are directly expressible.
Scalability and semantic coverage depend on tool and network complexity.

established_findings.statement: LLMs and LLM-integrated systems exhibit documented failure modes relevant to NetOps, including hallucinations, incorrect/safety-critical outputs, and vulnerability to prompt-injection or indirect prompt attacks.
limitations: Security/attack studies are general to LLM-integrated applications; NetOps-specific exploit demonstrations are limited in the supplied records.
Defensive efficacy evaluations are often on synthetic or constrained datasets.

established_findings.statement: Generate–validate–repair (tool-assisted) architectures — i.e., LLMs taught or orchestrated to call verifiers/tools and then repair based on feedback — are a promising mitigation and have been demonstrated to improve outcomes in prototype studies.
limitations: Demonstrations are prototype-scale and do not establish full automation without human oversight.
Effectiveness depends on quality of verifier feedback and specification granularity.

established_findings.statement: Surveys and domain reviews report growing research activity on applying LLMs to NetOps/AIOps/telecommunications and identify fragmented evaluation practices and a need for more operationally meaningful benchmarks and metrics.
limitations: Surveys synthesize existing literature but do not provide unified empirical benchmarks themselves.
Rapid field evolution may outpace survey coverage.

unresolved_questions.statement: Whether LLM-based NetOps systems (generate+verify+repair) achieve production-ready reliability and safety across diverse, large-scale, multi-vendor operational networks remains unresolved.
limitations: Available records describe prototypes, proposals, or limited-scale experiments rather than validated production deployments.
Claims of feasibility in preprints are not equivalent to rigorous production evaluation.

unresolved_questions.statement: To what extent LLM+verifier approaches generalize quantitatively across many vendors, protocols (BGP, MPLS, vendor-specific CLIs), and large topologies is not established by the supplied records.
limitations: Reported experiments target specific tasks/use-cases; broader generalization requires larger, diverse benchmarks and evaluations.

candidate_gaps.statement: A gap exists for standardized, operationally grounded benchmarks and metrics that measure configuration correctness, safety, and deployability (not just syntactic or reference-match accuracy) for LLM-driven NetOps.
limitations: Some benchmark proposals exist (e.g., NetConfEval) but broader community adoption and operational validity remain open.

candidate_gaps.statement: Scalable, low-human-overhead methods for closing the loop (automated localized repair guided by verifiers) that retain safety guarantees under diverse network semantics are underexplored.
limitations: Existing demonstrations show benefit but are prototype-level and rely on human verification for critical steps.

candidate_gaps.statement: Research gap: defenses and robust architectures specifically addressing prompt-injection and indirect prompt attacks in NetOps contexts (where maliciously crafted inputs could cause unsafe configurations) need focused study and rigorous mitigation evaluation.
limitations: Attack analyses are general to LLM-integrated apps; NetOps-specific threat models and mitigations require targeted research.

excluded_claims: LLMs are currently production-ready for fully autonomous, unsupervised NetOps in diverse, real-world networks (unsupported by the supplied records).
This record set provides evidence that any single LLM is universally superior for NetOps tasks across vendors and protocols (no supplied multi-model, multi-vendor superiority evidence).
Pre-lock development artifacts or rehearsals constitute empirical evidence for final autonomous-run outcomes (excluded per the supplied records and constraints).
